reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) strongly supports the mechanism by which heterogeneous grain structures improve mechanical properties in a low-SFE alloy, but all passages come from a single paper on a different alloy system (CrCoNi) and provide no direct evidence that such processing preserves caloric performance or is applicable to the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 system. The key premise linking HGS to unchanged caloric response is entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Heterogeneous grain structures (HGS) enhance strain hardening and ductility via back stresses and strain gradients
Severe cold rolling followed by partial annealing can create a heterogeneous grain structure
Partial recrystallization preserves transformation-active coarse grains while introducing ultrafine grains
Improved mechanical integrity from HGS does not significantly degrade functional (caloric) properties
The processing window (annealing at ~0.9·T_transition) is feasible for this specific alloy system
